issues.description: Substring match in validate_conda accepts any path containing 'conda' or 'mamba' in its --version output
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"])` is a sloppy data check. Any tool whose version string happens to contain 'mamba' or 'conda' passes. Compare the basename of the executable, or parse the first token of stdout. The right data check is exact, not substring soup.

issues.description: Windows-only `*.exe` filter prevents selecting the executable on macOS and Linux
issues.detail: `filters='*.exe'` in create_browsefile means Linux/macOS users browsing for `conda`, `mamba`, or `micromamba` (no extension) see nothing. The filter should be platform-aware or omitted. Small data fact, large user impact.

issues.description: Empty-string sentinel for 'no custom conda' is a weak data structure
issues.detail: `conda_path: ''` plus a `custom_conda` boolean encodes the same state twice. validate_conda then special-cases `""` as valid. One field (Optional[str], None means unset) would make the algorithm self-evident and eliminate the dual-flag drift risk. Not blocking, but the data shape is fighting itself.

issues.description: Nested if/else for fallback path could be a flat lookup
issues.detail: The kernelspec change nests a conditional inside the `if not conda_exe` branch. A small helper — `conda_exe = find_conda() or _user_configured_conda()` — would make the data flow obvious: try discovery, then fall back to config, then error. Composition over nesting.

issues.description: validate_conda swallows exceptions silently, hiding diagnostic data
issues.detail: The bare `except Exception: return False` discards why validation failed (timeout, permission, decode error). At minimum log it; better, let the caller distinguish 'not a conda' from 'failed to run'. Data the user needs to debug their own config gets thrown away.

issues.description: setFocus() side effect added to a general-purpose helper for one caller's benefit
issues.detail: `select_file` in widgets/config.py now unconditionally calls `edit.setFocus()` after picking a file. That changes behavior for every existing browsefile in the app to serve this one new field. Either make it opt-in via a parameter or leave the shared helper alone — small composable tools should not grow per-caller side effects.

review.summary: The feature is small and the data flow is roughly right: a checkbox plus a path, falling back when discovery fails. But the data structure is slightly redundant (boolean + path encode the same state twice), and the validation does substring matching where exact matching belongs. The Windows-only file filter will silently break the picker on Linux and macOS. The kernelspec branch could be flattened into a clean fallback chain. None of this is heroic; it's small data hygiene and one cross-platform fact. TOO-CLEVER on the substring check, WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE on the dual-flag config, otherwise SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE.
